name: Rule of 40 (software)
summary: Technology companies whose revenue growth plus FCF margin is at least 40%.
how_to_read: The universe is limited to Glint's Technology sector, which is SIC-based, not GICS, so it includes hardware and semiconductor companies as well as software. Two filters must both pass: revenue growth (year on year) plus FCF margin of at least 40%, and TTM revenue of at least $500M so small companies with noisy percentages drop out. Versions of the rule use EBITDA margin or other profit margins. Glint uses FCF margin.
misses: Stock-based pay: FCF margin counts it as non-cash, so a company paying heavily in stock looks better here than it would after SBC. Check the SBC column.
Hardware and one-off sales businesses: the rule was written for subscription software and means less for them.
source: Feld, 'The Rule of 40% For a Healthy SaaS Company' (2015); SaaS industry heuristic
